producer_report.summary: Each build slot now owns a warm target directory at `<state>/build-slots/<n>/target`. It outlives jobs and is made by `ensure_slot_targets` in state.rs. When a local check wins slot n, the job's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` path (`{job_dir}/target/verify`) becomes a symlink to that directory for the one command. That is the new `BuildLink` guard in env.rs, which runs the lexical check on the path before linking. After the command the link is removed. Then `cargo clean --offline --target-dir <slot> -p <member>` runs for every workspace member, so workspace-crate output goes and third-party output stays. If cleaning fails, the slot directory is deleted instead. A slot directory over the new `[drain.pipeline] slot_max_gb` (default 8, at least 1) is deleted and remade before its next use, and a `disk` line says so. `Slot` now exposes `index()`. Tests cover reuse between two jobs, the size limit, real workspace cleaning, `BuildLink`, config validation and slot directories surviving job cleanup. The design note step 5 is marked Built and says what was not measured, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry. athena.toml and defaults.toml are unchanged.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core slots: a test runs two jobs' checks one after the other through the same slot and asserts both used the same slot directory path under build-slots/<n>/target, and that third-party output written by the first is still present for the second.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-core slot`. Test `two_jobs_reuse_the_same_build_slots_target_directory` in run/tests.rs passes. It runs two jobs through `go`. Each job's check reads the link at `{job_dir}/target/verify`. Both links point to `state.slot_target(0)`, which ends in build-slots/0/target. The second job sees `libserde-0123abcd.rlib` written by the first. `slots::tests::a_slot_knows_its_number_and_a_freed_number_is_taken_again` also passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: after a command, a test asserts the slot directory keeps third-party output and workspace-crate output is gone (cargo clean -p per workspace member, or an equivalent shown by the test).
criteria_check.evidence: Two tests pass. `slots::tests::cleaning_a_slot_drops_workspace_crate_output_and_keeps_third_party_output` runs a real cargo build of a one-crate workspace, then `clean_workspace_output`, and finds no file with 'alpha' in its name while the planted serde files remain. `run::tests::...::after_a_command_the_slot_keeps_third_party_output_and_loses_workspace_crate_output` does the same through the job path: debug/deps ends up holding only the third-party file, with no warning line.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test -p athena-core: a test makes a slot directory larger than slot_max_gb and asserts it is deleted and recreated empty before the next use, and one under the limit is kept.
criteria_check.evidence: `run::tests::...::a_slot_directory_over_slot_max_gb_is_deleted_before_the_next_use_and_one_under_it_is_kept` uses config slot_max_gb = 2 with a test-only shrunken gigabyte of 50 KB. Job 1 leaves 300 KB. Job 2 finds it deleted and empty, and a 'disk build slot 0 ... over its 2 GB limit' line is printed. Job 2 leaves 20 KB. Job 3 finds the 20 KB kept. `state::tests::a_slot_target_over_its_limit_is_deleted_and_made_empty_and_one_under_it_is_kept` checks the byte-level rule: at the limit it is kept, one byte over it is deleted, and only CACHEDIR.TAG is left. No test writes a real gigabyte.

criteria_check.criterion: Each of max_check_slots build slots owns one directory <state>/build-slots/<n>/target created in crates/athena-core/src/state.rs that is not removed when a job ends; the job's target path is linked to it only for the command's duration (read crates/athena-core/src/run/checks.rs and crates/athena-agent/src/env.rs).
criteria_check.evidence: state.rs has `slot_target`, `ensure_slot_targets(count)`, `prepare_slot_target` and `reset_slot_target`. run/mod.rs calls `ensure_slot_targets(max_check_slots)` before building the SnapExec. checks.rs `link_slot_target` creates an `env::BuildLink`, which is dropped right after the command, before the clean and the snapshot restore. `BuildLink` drop removes only the symlink. Tests: `slot_target_directories_outlive_jobs_and_are_made_once` shows `clean_job` leaves the slot directory; the env.rs link tests; the e2e tests assert the link is gone after each job.

open_issues: The second build's wall time in a warm slot and the slot's size after real jobs are not recorded anywhere. The design note says so. A later job should add them, for example to `measure-build` or the check record.
slot_max_gb defaults to 8, which is a guess above the 5 to 6 GB estimate in the design. No measurement backs it.
The size limit is checked before use, so an over-limit directory stays on disk until its slot is won again.
Baseline and fails-without reruns still do not use a slot, and so do not use the warm directory (out of scope, as before).
The CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG and CARGO_INCREMENTAL settings in athena.toml were not touched (the maintainer's separate job).

The link path is taken from the CARGO_TARGET_DIR environment value. A repository whose change capability sets no CARGO_TARGET_DIR gets no slot directory and builds in the job's own directory as before.
mistakes: The first version of the slot directory had no CACHEDIR.TAG, so `cargo clean` failed and the slot was deleted after every command. Found by the end-to-end test and fixed.
I tried to read the saved full-suite output, which the tools blocked (outside the working directory), so I could not read the per-test results.
learnings: `cargo clean` refuses a target directory without a `CACHEDIR.TAG` file. Cargo writes that file only into a directory it creates itself, so a slot directory made empty by Athena needs the tag written by Athena. My first version had no tag, and the e2e test showed it deleting the slot after every command.

The check in env.rs (`check_build_dirs`) is lexical, so a symlink at `{job_dir}/target/<side>` passes it. The test fake capability returned an empty env, so I made it return the same `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` template as athena.toml. Other tests that run through `go` now also take the link path.
Jobs run one after another in a test from the same base commit make 'no change' unless the producer's edit differs. I added `each_job_its_own_edit` to give each job its own README text.
`cargo clean -p` removes deps files by computed hash, so planted fake workspace files would not be removed. Tests build for real instead.
desires: A way to read the output of a large `cargo test` run. I could not read the saved result file, so I could not check per-test results of the full suite.
A way to measure the second-build time in a warm slot against a real workspace.
